articles.title: Pakistan launches deadly air strikes on Afghanistan
articles.summary: The Afghan Taliban says nine civilians have died while Pakistan says the strikes killed 22 militants.
articles.body:
Pakistan has conducted further air strikes on Afghanistan, killing nine civilians and injuring 11 others, the Taliban government said.

Islamabad's information ministry confirmed the strikes, which it said killed twenty-two militants.

Zabihullah Mujahid, the chief spokesman of the Afghan Taliban, said the strikes hit homes in the Kunar and Helmand provinces bordering Pakistan. Women and children are among the dead, he said in an X post.

"We condemn this act as an aggression and crime in violation of all accepted principles," he said.

Pakistan had very different claims, saying that the "well-planned and calibrated" attack targeted "terrorist camps" in Afghanistan, where large quantities of weapons and ammunition were stored.

Maximum precautions were taken to ensure no collateral damage occurred, Pakistan's information ministry said.

An eyewitness from Garmsir, Qudratullah, told the BBC that the airstrikes started around 03:30 local time (00:00 BST) and continued for 30 minutes.

"We were sleeping when the jets arrived. After the first bomb exploded, we woke up. After the second strikes, we took our children and fled the area. The third bomb hit our neighbours house; between four and give members of their family were killed while others were injured and taken to hospital."

Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban of harbouring militant groups that carry out and plan attacks on it from inside Afghanistan's territory.

The Afghan Taliban deny it, saying Pakistan's militancy is an internal problem, but it has led to a significant deterioration in the relationship between the two neighbours.

Fighting between the neighbours escalated dramatically in February this year, with Pakistan declaring that it's in an "open war" with Afghanistan after a surge in deadly clashes and cross-border airstrikes.

Talks mediated by China established a fragile ceasefire in March, but it did nolast.

Last month, a deadly attack on a police facility in north-west Pakistan, which killed 24 people, was blamed on the Pakistani Taliban by the provincial police force.

Last week, Pakistan launched air strikes in Afghanistan which hit Kandahar, the Taliban's base of power, among other provinces. This earlier attack killed four civilians , according to the Afghan Taliban government.

articles.title: FDA finds potential source of cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to lettuce
articles.summary: The FDA said two samples tested positive for the parasite.
articles.body:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) said on Friday it has found a potential source of the cyclosporiasis outbreak that was tied to lettuce over the summer.

The agency collected samples during its onsite inspections of Taylor Farms de Mexico facilities, it said.

Two samples tested positive for the parasite, Cyclospora, according to the FDA. One positive sample was from a tank that held outgoing wastewater from a processing facility, the agency said. The second positive sample was from a drainage ditch of an iceberg lettuce grower, it noted.

"While there is currently not enough evidence to conclusively determine how contamination occurred in this outbreak, the positive samples show that Cyclospora was present in the environment where lettuce was grown and processed," the FDA wrote in an update on its website .

"This adds to the strong epidemiological data and traceback convergence supporting the link between this outbreak and recalled shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico," the update continued.

The FDA said its investigation has closed. Health officials say they are confident that all recalled lettuce associated with this outbreak is off the market.

In a statement, a Taylor Fresh Foods spokesperson said its facility in central Mexico remains closed as the company works with its research team to implement enhanced safety protocols.

"The independent grower where a positive sample was found is no longer part of our supplier program," the spokesperson said. "The sample FDA referenced came from discharged waste and sewer water outside of our processing facility. As FDA noted in its report, there is currently not enough evidence to conclusively determine how contamination occurred or how results for these samples relate to ongoing genotyping of clinical specimens."

The statement concluded: "We remain concerned for the people and families impacted by this outbreak. Millions of families rely on the safety of Taylor Farms produce and we take that responsibility seriously. We know trust is earned by what we do, and we will continue to learn, improve and take action to keep our food fresh and safe."

At least 12,883 people were infected with cyclosporiasis across 21 states after eating the recalled lettuce, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Thousands more cases were reported but health officials noted difficulties in tying infections to the recalled foods.

A total of 570 people were hospitalized and two people in Michigan died.

In mid-July, the FDA and the CDC announced they were investigating a multi-state outbreak of cyclosporiasis illnesses linked to shredded iceberg lettuce served at some Taco Bell restaurants.

The lettuce was supplied to Taco Bell by Taylor Farms and sourced from central Mexico.

Taylor Farms de Mexico issued a voluntary recall of all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico, with the recall affecting 27 states. The recalled products were distributed from June 29 through July 16 and have best-if-used-by dates up to Aug. 3.

Taco Bell said it is no longer using lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico at any of its restaurants.

articles.title: Ronaldo Caiado, candidato à Presidência pelo PSD, cumpre agenda em Goiás | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato disse que, se eleito, vai focar no combate à corrupção e à violência.
articles.summary: Candidato disse que, se eleito, vai focar no combate à corrupção e à violência.
articles.body:
Ronaldo Caiado , do PSD , teve agenda em Goiás.

Ronaldo Caiado começou o dia caminhando pela região central de Goiânia. Cumprimentou e conversou com apoiadores. Disse que, se eleito, vai focar no combate à corrupção e à violência:

“Tem que ter essa autoridade moral e coragem pessoal para enfrentar o crime e a corrupção no Brasil. E isso eu já deixei claro que eu tenho de sobra para poder corrigir isso. Me empreste aí a sua coragem, me dê a eleição que você vai ver que eu vou devolver o Brasil aos brasileiros de bem”.

Depois, o candidato do PSD seguiu para a região noroeste da capital, onde participou de uma carreata. No fim da tarde, Ronaldo Caiado foi para Trindade, cidade conhecida como a capital da fé em Goiás, para o último compromisso de campanha. O candidato se reuniu com eleitores na Praça do Santuário Basílica do Divino Pai Eterno, fez uma caminhada e encerrou a campanha em uma celebração na Igreja Matriz de Trindade.

articles.title: PI tem 210 denúncias de propaganda irregular na véspera da eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Aplicativo Pardal, da Justiça Eleitoral, registrou ocorrências em 31 municípios; propaganda irregular na internet foi a infração mais denunciada.
articles.summary: Aplicativo Pardal, da Justiça Eleitoral, registrou ocorrências em 31 municípios; propaganda irregular na internet foi a infração mais denunciada.
articles.body:
Neste sábado (3), véspera do 1º turno das eleições 2026, o Aplicativo Pardal soma 210 denúncias de irregularidades na propaganda eleitoral no Piauí.

🐦‍⬛⚠️ O Pardal é uma ferramenta da Justiça Eleitoral que permite aos cidadãos denunciar possíveis irregularidades na propaganda eleitoral durante a campanha. O sistema busca ampliar a participação popular e contribuir para a transparência do processo eleitoral.

Segundo a Justiça Eleitoral, as denúncias foram registradas em 31 municípios piauienses. Teresina concentra a maior parte dos casos, com 105 registros. Em seguida aparecem Parnaíba, com 35 denúncias, e Piripiri, com 13.

Valença do Piauí, Campo Maior, Barras, Altos, Amarante, Bom Jesus e Esperantina registram menos de 10 denúncias cada.

A propaganda irregular na internet foi o tipo de ocorrência mais denunciado, com 37 registros. Em seguida, aparecem os casos relacionados ao uso de carro de som, minitrio ou trio elétrico, com 35 denúncias. Veja mais:

Os candidatos a deputado estadual são os principais alvos das denúncias, com 87 registros. Em seguida, aparecem os candidatos a deputado federal, com 47 denúncias.

Também foram registradas 15 denúncias contra candidatos ao governo do estado, seis contra candidatos ao Senado e quatro contra candidatos à Presidência da República.

Além disso, 51 denúncias tiveram como alvo partidos, coligações ou federações.

A divulgação dos dados não permite o acesso ao nome dos candidatos, partidos, coligações ou federações denunciados.

O aplicativo Pardal está disponível gratuitamente para download nas lojas App Store e Google Play . Por meio da plataforma, os eleitores podem registrar denúncias sobre possíveis irregularidades na propaganda eleitoral.

Para fazer uma denúncia, o cidadão deve se identificar por meio de autenticação no e-Título ou na plataforma Gov.br.

A denúncia deve conter informações que permitam identificar e apurar a possível irregularidade. Também é possível anexar fotos, vídeos e áudios para ajudar na comprovação do caso.

articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada neste sábado (3), véspera do 1º turno, mostra como está a disputa pelo governo do Tocantins. A candidata Professora Dorinha (União) aparece na frente com 46% dos votos válidos, seguido pelo candidato Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) com 41% e pelo candidato Laurez Moreira (PSD) com 11%.

📲 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O candidato José Wilson Siqueira Campos Júnior (Democrata) renunciou à candidatura ao governo do Tocantins e, neste sábado (3), declarou apoio à Professora Dorinha (União). O anúncio foi feito em um vídeo publicado pela candidata nas redes sociais.

Segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral (TRE-TO), o nome do candidato permanece na urna porque os dados já haviam sido carregados. Porém, os votos eventualmente registrados para ele não serão contabilizados na totalização nem no resultado final da eleição.

Siqueira Júnior entrou na disputa no início de setembro, após o TRE-TO indeferir o registro da candidatura de Luiz Carlos Ferreira da Silva e do vice, Jair Medeiros.

É a forma como o TSE divulga o resultado oficial das eleições. São os votos dados nos candidatos. Esse cálculo deixa de fora os votos em branco e nulos e abstenções. Para vencer no 1º turno, um candidato precisa de 50% dos votos válidos mais um voto.

Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

A Quaest leva em consideração as intenções de voto da pesquisa e o perfil de comparecimento para estimar os votos válidos. É o modelo likely voter, que considera eleitores com maior propensão a votar.

O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Anhanguera e ouviu 1.800 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 2 e 3 de outubro. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número TO-01946/2026.

Veja agora o resultado com os votos totais, incluindo votos em branco, nulos e eleitores indecisos.

Veja agora a pesquisa espontânea, em que os eleitores respondem sem ter acesso a uma lista de candidatos.

Esses resultados ajudam a medir o grau de consolidação do voto. Quanto maior o número de indecisos na véspera, menos consolidado está o voto e maior a possibilidade de mudanças em relação ao resultado de domingo.

Entre os eleitores que declaram voto em um candidato, 82% dizem que a decisão é definitiva. Outros 17% afirmam que ainda podem mudar de ideia.

articles.title: Sorocaba e Jundiaí têm chances de chuva no fim de semana das eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Fim de semana deve ser de muitas nuvens e pancadas de chuva, inclusive no domingo (4) de votação, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).
articles.summary: A Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo indicou um aumento da nebulosidade e da ocorrência de pancadas de chuva no fim de semana, inclusive no domingo, dia do 1º turno das eleições.
articles.body:
Estão previstas muitas nuvens e pancadas de chuva para o fim de semana em Sorocaba (SP), incluindo o domingo (4), dia do 1º turno das eleições — Foto: Reprodução/Kelly Rosa Baptista

A Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo indicou um aumento da nebulosidade e da ocorrência de pancadas de chuva no fim de semana, inclusive no domingo (4), dia do 1º turno das Eleições 2026, para as regiões de Sorocaba e Jundiaí .

Segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), em Sorocaba (SP), o sábado (3) deve ser de muitas nuvens e chances de pancadas de chuva à tarde e à noite. As temperaturas devem variar entre 17°C e 24°C. Não há previsão de tempestades severas para o estado.

No domingo, dia em que os eleitores vão às urnas, o céu deve ficar coberto por nuvens e há chances de pancadas de chuva e trovoadas. Os termômetros devem oscilar entre 16°C e 27°C.

Condições meteorológicas semelhantes também devem ser registradas no início da próxima semana. Na segunda-feira (5), estão previstas pancadas de chuva e trovoadas, além de céu encoberto por nuvens. A temperatura mínima do dia deve ser de 18°C e a máxima de 27°C.

Pode haver uma queda de temperatura na terça-feira (6), com os termômetros variando entre 18°C e 22°C. Novamente, o dia deve ter pancadas de chuva e trovoadas.

Jundiaí (SP) também deve registrar aumento de nebulosidade e pancadas de chuva nos próximos dias. No sábado, os termômetros devem variar entre 14°C e 23°C.

No dia da eleição, o jundiaiense deve ir às urnas em um dia com muitas nuvens e pancadas de chuva. As temperaturas oscilam entre 17°C e 25°C.

Um ligeiro aumento de temperatura pode ser registrado na segunda-feira, com oscilações ao longo do dia entre 18°C e 27°C. Na terça, os termômetros devem sair dos 16°C e podem chegar aos 21°C.

articles.title: Trump anuncia pagamento de US$ 90 a idosos antes das eleições nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 20 milhões de beneficiários do programa público de saúde Medicare receberão pagamento único em outubro; anúncio ocorre um mês antes das eleições de meio de mandato.
articles.summary: Trump anunciou pagamento único de US$ 90 para mais de 20 milhões de idosos do Medicare. Benefício será distribuído em outubro, antes das eleições.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , anunciou um pagamento de US$ 90 (equivalentes a R$ 468,97) para mais de 20 milhões de idosos que recebem o Medicare, programa público de saúde americano.

O dinheiro será destinado ao pagamento de parte dos custos do seguro e deve ser distribuído em outubro, poucas semanas antes das eleições de meio de mandato, marcadas para 3 de novembro.

O anúncio foi feito por Trump na noite da última sexta-feira (2), em uma publicação na Truth Social. O presidente já havia anunciado, no mês passado, que cerca de 1 milhão de pessoas receberiam cheques de US$ 500 (R$ 2.605) para ajudar a pagar os prêmios de planos de saúde vinculados ao Affordable Care Act, conhecido como Obamacare.

Trump também prometeu enviar US$ 5 mil para cada adulto americano caso os republicanos mantenham o controle da Câmara e do Senado nas eleições de meio de mandato . A medida dependeria de aprovação do Congresso e poderia custar mais de US$ 1 trilhão, aumentando o déficit público e pressionando a inflação.

A série de anúncios ocorre em um momento em que pesquisas mostram aumento da insatisfação dos americanos com o custo de vida. Apenas 17% aprovam a atuação de Trump no combate à inflação . O presidente tem sido responsabilizado por parte da população pelos preços elevados da gasolina e dos alimentos, enquanto afirma que a economia americana está em forte crescimento.

Segundo a Casa Branca, os pagamentos de US$ 90 serão financiados pelo Medicare Improvement Fund, fundo criado pelo Congresso em 2008 para financiar melhorias no funcionamento do Medicare e nos pagamentos a prestadores de serviços de saúde.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, discursa na 81ª Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas na sede da ONU em Nova York, em 22 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: ANGELA WEISS/AFP

Administrações anteriores não utilizaram o Medicare Improvement Fund para fazer pagamentos desse tipo. O Congresso, porém, já retirou recursos do fundo para financiar outras iniciativas.

Em 2010, por exemplo, US$ 20,74 bilhões foram usados para financiar a criação do Affordable Care Act.

Segundo Larry Levitt, vice-presidente executivo de política de saúde da KFF, a legislação que regulamenta o fundo dá ao governo ampla margem para decidir como utilizar os recursos.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Apple has removed Jack Dorsey-backed decentralised messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store following a government direction.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Apple has removed Jack Dorsey-backed decentralised messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store following a government direction. Dorsey shared a screenshot of Apple’s communication on X, which said the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) had sought the app’s removal under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000.According to the notice shared by Dorsey, the government told Apple that the app included content that was illegal in India and directed the company to make it unavailable to users in the country. Apple said in its communication that Bitchat would continue to remain available in other territories.The company also said that Bitchat’s TestFlight version, which allows developers to distribute beta versions of apps to users for testing, would no longer be available in India.Bitchat differs from conventional messaging platforms because it does not necessarily require users to connect to the internet or rely on centralised servers. The app uses Bluetooth-based mesh networking, allowing nearby devices to communicate directly with each other and relay messages across a network of connected devices.Its decentralised architecture and ability to enable communication even when conventional internet access is unavailable have brought the app under regulatory scrutiny in India.The latest removal means iPhone users in India can no longer download the app through the official App Store. Apple did not respond to queries sent by TOI on the government direction or the reasons cited for removing Bitchat from its India store.The order comes a day after protests were organised in Delhi and Mumbai by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The app, which can function without internet connectivity, had also faced a government takedown move in July, before again becoming available.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2017, Jimmy Carter leased 10 acres of his Georgia farm for a 1.3-megawatt solar project; it went on to generate about 60% of Plains' electricity demand
articles.summary: Before solar farms dotted the American landscape, Jimmy Carter was already threading renewable energy into his public legacy.
articles.body: Before solar farms dotted the American landscape, Jimmy Carter was already threading renewable energy into his public legacy. That philosophy was practiced in the past by the former president in his hometown of Plains, Georgia, where he leased part of his family farm for a solar project that would go on to provide a significant share of the small city’s electricity needs, an online report by Market Screener states.Solar project at Carter’s farmIn 2017, Carter leased 10 acres of his Georgia property to Atlanta-based SolAmerica Energy to build a 1.3-megawatt solar installation, according to Market Screener. The project was meant to provide over half of Plains’ electricity needs, a strikingly large renewable-energy installation for the community. Later estimates put its contribution at about 60% of the city's electricity demand.The report said the solar array was equipped with single-axis tracking technology, which means its panels are able to follow the movement of the sun and improve energy generation throughout the day. The project was developed, engineered and installed by SolAmerica and supported by a 25-year power purchase agreement with Georgia Power.More than 55 million kilowatt hoursThe Plains installation is expected to produce more than 55 million kilowatt-hours of clean electricity in its first 25 years. This was a sizable project for a community with a small population and relatively small electricity demand. The solar farm became part of Plains’ daily power supply rather than a demonstration installation. The project also typified a larger shift taking place in Georgia as utility-scale and distributed solar developments started to take off.The installation had an added historical dimension because it was located on land associated with Carter. Carter spent decades advocating for renewable energy, both while president and after leaving the White House.Carter's legacy on renewable energyCarter’s interest in solar power is not new, dating back to his presidency from 1977 to 1981. His administration created the Department of Energy , and set policies that helped shape the emerging energy framework of the country . He also signed legislation called the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act, or PURPA, which helped spur greater participation by independent power producers and contributed to the growth of renewable energy in the United States.The report also notes that Carter became closely identified with solar energy during his presidency after solar panels were put on the White House. The panels were meant to show what solar power could do when the technology was still far from being common. Though the panels were removed during the Reagan administration, Carter’s legacy of renewable energy persisted long after his presidency.A local project with a global messageThe Plains installation linked that long-standing interest in renewable energy with Carter’s hometown. And its location on his property also highlighted the potential role that privately owned land can play in developing smaller, distributed energy projects. The long-term contract was expected to make the solar installation productive for decades, providing electricity and helping diversify the community’s sources of energy.For Plains the project was more than a solar array. It was a rare convergence of local history, energy policy and technological change. Once famous for its peanuts, agriculture and the former president’s post-White House life, Carter’s farm has another chapter as part of Georgia’s shift to renewable power. Beginning with 10 acres and a modest 1.3-megawatt installation, it became a major electricity provider for the town, a lasting testament to how a small community can take a familiar piece of landscape and make it part of its energy future.Images Courtesy: Facebook and istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: Indians live longer than Pakistanis, lag Bangladeshis, says WHO
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indians can expect to live longer than their counterparts in Pakistan, but have shorter lives than people in Bangladesh, the US and Canada,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indians can expect to live longer than their counterparts in Pakistan, but have shorter lives than people in Bangladesh, the US and Canada, according to the latest World Health Organization estimates.India's life expectancy at birth was 71 years in 2023, compared with 68.2 years in Pakistan, 72.7 years in Bangladesh, 78.5 years in the US and 81.4 years in Canada. But living longer does not necessarily mean living more years in good health. India's healthy life expectancy was 60.6 years in 2023, compared with 60.5 in 2019. It had fallen to 58.4 years in 2021 before recovering to 60.2 years in 2022. The figures are part of WHO's Global Health Estimates, released Friday, covering life expectancy, healthy life expectancy, causes of death and disease burden from 2000 to 2023. WHO said global life expectancy recovered close to pre-pandemic levels, while healthy life expectancy has recovered more slowly.In 2 years from 2021, India regained 2.9 years of expected lifespan: WHOFor India, the difference is particularly visible over the pandemic years. Life expectancy fell from 70.5 years in 2019 to 68.1 years in 2021 before rising to 70.5 years in 2022 and 71 years in 2023. In just two years, India regained 2.9 years of expected lifespan.Healthy life expectancy, however, recovered by only 2.2 years, from 58.4 years in 2021 to 60.6 years in 2023, leaving it just 0.1 year above the 2019 level.The gap is also visible among older Indians. At age 60, a person could expect another 18.8 years of life in 2023, compared with 18.4 years in 2019. But 13.7 of those years were expected to be lived in full health, up from 13.4 years in 2019.India’s disease profile has changed sharply. Communicable diseases, such as tuberculosis and diarrhoeal infections, can spread from person to person, while non-communicable diseases (NCDs), such as heart disease, stroke and diabetes, are generally long-term conditions.In 2000, communicable diseases accounted for nearly 62% of the combined death rate from the country’s 10 leading causes, while NCDs accounted for 34%. By 2023, the pattern had reversed, with NCDs accounting for nearly 75% and communicable diseases 16% of the combined death rate from the top 10 causes. The rest was from injuries.The shift is evident in the leading causes. In 2000, tuberculosis and diarrhoeal diseases topped the list, with 92.4 and 87.8 deaths per 100,000 population. By 2023, ischaemic heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, stroke and diabetes were among the leading causes, with rates of 138.5, 83.19, 74.8 and 49.01, respectively. Yet infectious diseases remain a significant burden, with diarrhoeal diseases, tuberculosis and lower respiratory infections still among India’s top 10 causes of death in 2023.Globally, the shift towards chronic diseases is also pronounced. NCDs accounted for 74% of deaths in 2023, up from 58% in 2000, while eight of the world’s 10 leading causes of death were NCDs. Global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, almost back to the 73.4 years recorded in 2019, while healthy life expectancy stood at 62.8 years, still 0.4 years below its 2019 level.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Hormuz blocked, but Gulf crude shipments at pre-war level
articles.summary: Disruptions to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz notwithstanding, crude shipments from the West Asian Gulf region, excluding Iran, have
articles.body: Disruptions to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz notwithstanding, crude shipments from the West Asian Gulf region, excluding Iran, have returned to pre-war levels as countries cut dependence on oil tankers to navigate through the choked strait. According to maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler, at least 16.5 million barrels per day (mbd) of crude left the region between Sept 1 and 28, matching the prewar average. During the peak of the West Asia war in March, the average was 10.5 mbd.While 83% of the region’s crude crossed Hormuz before the war, 40% was exported in Sept through pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the UAE without crossing the key chokepoint.Of the remaining 60% that physically crossed Hormuz, most was moved using shuttle tankers, Emmanuel Belostrino, head of global crude and geopolitical market data at Kpler, said in his analysis.Belostrino said more than 70% of the crude that crossed the Strait of Hormuz in Aug changed tankers offshore in the Gulf of Oman.Crude via other routes made up the differenceConfirmed crude crossings were still more than a quarter below the pre-war level, but volumes moving through alternative routes had more than doubled and made up almost exactly the difference. Saudi pushed more crude through the east-west pipeline to Yanbu, with loadings rising from 0.8 mbd before the war to 4.3 mbd in June. UAE sent crude through the Abu Dhabi crude oil pipeline to Fujairah, where loadings rose from 1.1 mbd to 2.7 mbd.325 million barrels released from oil reserves: IEAThe International Energy Agency said member countries had released 325 million barrels of oil and oil products from strategic reserves, out of 400 million barrels pledged in March.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Finance system resilient, economy braved West Asia crisis: RBI governor
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday said the Indian financial system remained resilient and the economy had navigated the West Asia crisis
articles.body: NEW DELHI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday said the Indian financial system remained resilient and the economy had navigated the West Asia crisis well, but policymakers needed to stay vigilant."We cannot afford to become complacent; the economic and financial costs of allowing vulnerabilities to build up are simply too high... Today's resilience may not necessarily imply tomorrow's immunity. We are committed to remaining vigilant of emerging vulnerabilities and continuing to keep our financial system strong and resilient," he said at the Kautilya Economic Conclave, organised by the Institute of Economic Growth and the finance ministry.He cautioned against the possible adverse impact of the war in Iran, which has hit supply chains. "The financial system has absorbed the supply shock due to the West Asia conflict well. However, the global economic environment remains challenging. The conflict has exacerbated inflationary pressures and enhanced financial system vulnerabilities," the RBI governor said, adding India was navigating from a position of strength.Malhotra cautioned against stressed valuations, especially those related to AI, elevated debt levels globally, elevated leverage that could spill over to banks and markets in case of tightening of financial conditions, private credit, and cyber risks that have been compounded by AI."Strong macroeconomic fundamentals and a resilient financial system provide confidence in our ability to withstand this lingering shock. At the same time, we are taking further measures to enhance our resilience to such shocks," he said, listing diversification of import sources, greater self-sufficiency in energy and other critical resources, enhancing manufacturing competitiveness, expanding market access through free trade agreements, and promoting trade settlement in local currencies, among others.The RBI governor also said Indian bond yields had risen only partially in response to higher global energy prices and global yields, reflecting the prudence in fiscal management, credible monetary policy and declining structural pressure on inflation.He said the Indian private credit market remained small, equity markets had corrected in recent months, and cyber risk governance had been strengthened. articles.title: Kristin Davis helped rescue one-year-old elephant after finding her alone in Kenya; years later, Chaimu returned to the wild and inspired a sculpture
articles.summary: In 2009, a holiday in Kenya brought actress Kristin Davis into an unexpected encounter with an abandoned elephant calf.
articles.body: In 2009, a holiday in Kenya brought actress Kristin Davis into an unexpected encounter with an abandoned elephant calf. While staying in the Chyulu Hills, Davis and staff from Kampi Ya Kanzi came across the young elephant on its own. When the calf was still without its mother several days later, a decision was made to intervene. The orphan, later named Chaimu, was about a year old and was taken into the care of the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, now known as the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust. Sixteen years on, Chaimu has become part of a very different story. After years of rehabilitation and time learning alongside wild elephants, she has returned to the wild.Kristin Davis helps rescue an abandoned elephant calf in KenyaDavis was holidaying in the Chyulu Hills when she and people working at Kampi Ya Kanzi spotted the calf. At first, there was uncertainty over whether the elephant had simply become separated from its herd. But the situation did not change over the following days.With the calf continuing to remain alone, the group decided that intervention was necessary. The DSWT was contacted and arrangements were made to rescue the young elephant. She was named Chaimu and, at roughly one year old, began a rehabilitation process that would eventually take her from the Nairobi Nursery to the organisation’s reintegration programme in Tsavo East.From the nursery to Tsavo East: Chaimu learns life among wild elephantsChaimu’s care did not end with her arrival at the Nairobi Nursery. Orphaned elephants in rehabilitation need to develop many of the behaviours they would ordinarily learn from their families, including how to interact with other elephants and function within a herd.After graduating from the nursery, Chaimu moved to the Ithumba Reintegration Centre in Tsavo East. The centre allows older orphan elephants to spend increasing amounts of time around wild elephants before making the transition away from human care.That process was reflected in Davis’s later descriptions of Chaimu. The elephant was regularly mixing with wild herds and learning the skills needed for life outside the sanctuary system.A 2011 Kenya visit strengthens Davis’s ties to elephant conservationThe encounter did not become an isolated episode in Davis’s life. She continued supporting the organisation and used her public profile to draw attention to its work with orphaned elephants and wider conservation issues.Her involvement included visits to Kenya. In July 2011, she returned with her friend Ame and filmmaker Roz Edwards, spending time at the Nairobi Nursery before travelling to Ithumba in Tsavo East. During that visit, she stayed at Ithumba Camp, which had been established alongside the reintegration centre and was intended to support limited responsible tourism in the northern part of Tsavo East.Davis also spoke publicly about Chaimu and the charity’s work, including an appearance on The Oprah Winfrey Show. She has continued to identify elephant conservation and the illegal ivory trade among the issues she has highlighted.A longer commitment to wildlife conservationDavis’s work with elephants has since extended beyond her connection with Chaimu. She also served as a Goodwill Ambassador for UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, in 2017, according to The UN Refugee Agency.Her interest in conservation has also crossed into film. The Perfect World Foundation Award says that in 2014, she executive produced and financed Gardeners of Eden, a documentary about the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust and its efforts to protect elephants. The film received recognition at several film festivals, including the Elephant Hero Award at the UN-sponsored International Elephant Film Festival in 2016, and was later a finalist for a Peabody Award.In September 2023, Davis received The Perfect World Foundation Award for her contribution to raising awareness around wildlife and biodiversity conservation.Chaimu becomes part of a larger conservation projectYears after the original rescue, Chaimu’s story became connected to The Great Elephant Migration, a conservation art project involving a travelling collection of elephant sculptures. Davis has supported the project and said she wanted to help raise awareness and funds for conservation work.A sculpture representing Chaimu is part of the migrating herd. Its inclusion links the animal Davis encountered as an orphaned calf in Kenya with the elephant she later saw progressing through rehabilitation and towards life in the wild.By then, Chaimu was 16 years old and had been reintegrated into the wild. Her story therefore spans much more than the original rescue. It covers the long period between being found alone in the Chyulu Hills and eventually becoming capable of living beyond the protection of the rehabilitation programme.From an orphaned calf to life in the wildChaimu’s journey illustrates the lengthy nature of elephant rehabilitation. The rescue itself happened quickly once it became clear that the calf was not being reunited with her herd, but the process that followed took years.From the Nairobi Nursery to Ithumba, Chaimu gradually spent more time in an environment where wild elephants could provide experiences and social interactions that a young orphan would otherwise have gained from its family. Her eventual return to the wild marked the later stage of that process.For Davis, the connection began with an encounter during a Kenyan holiday in 2009. More than a decade later, Chaimu’s name remains attached to her conservation work, this time through a sculpture travelling with The Great Elephant Migration and representing an elephant that survived the loss of its original herd and went on to rejoin wild elephants.You use AI every day. articles.title: Rs 3,750 crore RCom fraud: CBI names ex-LIC executive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: CBI has filed a chargesheet against Reliance Communications Ltd and three key executives in a Rs 3,750 crore fraud case alleged by Life
articles.body: NEW DELHI: CBI has filed a chargesheet against Reliance Communications Ltd and three key executives in a Rs 3,750 crore fraud case alleged by Life Insurance Corporation (LIC). The document names Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, Group MD of Reliance ADA Group, Vishwas Joshi, senior VP of Reliance Capital Limited, and P Venugopal, the then chief investment officer of LIC. articles.title: Father and son smoke shop workers arrested in Mississippi students' suspected kratom deaths
articles.summary: They are accused of selling at least one student derivatives of kratom, often called "gas station heroin" in the US.
articles.body:
A father and son who worked at a Mississippi smoke shop have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of at least one university student who died from a suspected overdose of kratom, sometimes called "gas station heroin" in the US.

The pair worked at a shop that allegedly sold derivatives of the substance to University of Mississippi students.

US prosecutors charged Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, for possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with the death investigation of two Ole Miss students last month.

Although their deaths have not officially been attributed to kratom, officials afterward issued warnings about consuming kratom .

The criminal complaint alleges that on 21 September, an Ole Miss student was found dead in his dorm room. The apparent cause of death "appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose", the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Mississippi said in a press release.

Law enforcement found packages - with some tablets missing - of suspected kratom derivatives.

About an hour later, a second student was found dead from a suspected overdose in another location, also with packages of suspected kratom derivatives.

Officials connected the packages with the local vape, tobacco and beer store, the US Attorney's statement said.

Law enforcement executed search warrants and seized suspected kratom derivative controlled substances from the store. The Mosleh's, father and son, were later arrested.

The two students' deaths have sparked alarm and warnings from officials about the plant-based drug referred to as "gas station heroin".

Kratom - a herb with opioid-like effects - has grown in popularity in the US over the last decade, and is typically purchased over the counter and consumed in pill or liquid form.

For years, anti-kratom advocates have pushed for bans, and in some countries, like the UK, it is illegal. But Kratom is not regulated by the US Food and Drug Administration and is legal in some states, including Mississippi.

The Mississippi prosecutors said that kratom derivatives, such as MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16, are now schedule I controlled substances in the US and can be significantly more potent than natural kratom leaf products and morphine.

articles.title: Insurance companies want policyholders to pay 10% of health claims
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Non-life insurers are considering a 10% co-payment by policyholders on retail health policies from Jan 1, 2027, with the patient's contribution
articles.body: MUMBAI: Non-life insurers are considering a 10% co-payment by policyholders on retail health policies from Jan 1, 2027, with the patient's contribution capped at Rs 5 lakh per claim. In return, customers would pay lower annual premiums.The proposal, being considered by the General Insurance Council, would pair the change with common hospital empanelment and a formal mechanism for settling disputes between insurers and hospitals. The arrangement would require even those with comprehensive health insurance to keep funds for medical emergencies, as they would have to pay 10% of admissible inpatient hospitalisation costs, including those arising from accidents, whether claims are settled through cashless procedure or reimbursement.Outpatient claims would remain outside schemeThe proposal covers retail indemnity products, retail-under-group policies, indemnity components of combi products, internal migrations and portability business. Outpatient claims would remain outside the scheme.Co-payment cannot be waived, reduced or modified through riders or endorsements, and the customer’s 10% contribution cannot be recovered from another health insurance policy.“The choice between a cheaper policy with a deductible and a full-compensation policy should rest with the insured. People buy insurance to be indemnified for their costs. It would be unfair to customers willing to pay a higher premium for a higher sum insured to still bear part of the cost, and this could discourage them from buying high-value policies,” said Shreeraj Deshpande, a health insurance expert who earlier headed operations at a general insurer. While the industry is seeking to address what it sees as cost distortions in healthcare, some fear a mandatory requirement could be anti-competitive. “If the industry collectively decides that no one will offer a full-compensation policy, it might catch the attention of the Competition Commission,” said an industry executive.The logic behind the measure is that hospitals may order additional diagnostic tests, recommend procedures and extend hospital stays when patients have comprehensive insurance cover. Higher-category rooms can also increase total bills because doctors’ fees and procedure charges are often linked to room tariffs. With insurance covering the full bill, patients may have less incentive to question charges or choose lower-cost hospitals.“This behaviour (overbilling and provider-induced demand) stems from the perception that insurance-backed patients are less price-sensitive, leading to inflated healthcare costs,” a council note said.The proposal also calls for common hospital empanelment, outcome-based contracts and a payor-provider grievance forum. GI Council plans standard empanelment across more than 4,300 hospitals to set benchmark tariffs and curb arbitrary billing, while linking contracts to clinical and procedure-wise outcomes.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Air ambulance missing on flight from Bermuda to Boston
articles.summary: The US coastguard says it has dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket.
articles.body:
An air ambulance has gone missing while carrying six people on a flight from Bermuda to Boston.

The US Federal Aviation Administration told the coastguard early on Saturday that it had lost contact with the plane, a Gulfstream jet, ⁠a coastguard spokesperson told the Reuters news agency by email.

The ⁠coastguard said it dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket, an island community south of mainland Massachusetts.

The National Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information about the situation on Saturday morning but had no further update to share.

The Canadian-registered air ambulance jet had four crew members and two passengers on board when it departed Bermuda’s LF Wade International airport overnight for the flight to Massachusetts, according to a statement from the Bermuda airport’s operator, Skyport.

Canada’s Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon said in a social media post that four Canadians were on the plane.

“We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue ‌efforts continue,” MacKinnon wrote.

The aircraft, registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, departed Bermuda at 12:41am local time (03:41 GMT), according to data from flight tracking website FlightAware.

The plane was flying at 24,000 feet (7,300 metres) for much of the flight before descending 13,000ft (3,960 metres) in about two minutes shortly before flight controllers lost contact, data showed.

Air traffic control audio posted by LiveATC.net offered a glimpse of the flight’s final communications before it went missing.

“Roger, you said you’re coming in blind. Is that what you said?” a controller can be heard asking the pilot.

The pilot’s transmission could not be heard in the recording. The controller later confirmed the pilot was declaring an emergency just before losing contact with the plane.

The Bermuda government is in contact with US ‌authorities and families of the passengers, Bermuda Premier David Burt wrote in a statement posted on Instagram.

“We are praying that all six people will ‌be ‌found safe,” he wrote.

Latitude Air Ambulance is based in Ontario, Canada, and provides medical evacuation services. The company ⁠did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: In 2021, Cambridge farmer Ben Webster spent £15,000 converting his sheep-grazing field that earned £300 a year into a private dog park; it now brings in up to £400 a week
articles.summary: Anything for the pets, isn’t it? In the UK, dog owners are paying by the hour for private, secure fields where their dogs can run freely and safely.
articles.body: Anything for the pets, isn’t it? In the UK, dog owners are paying by the hour for private, secure fields where their dogs can run freely and safely. Rebecca Lee, who lives in rural Cambridgeshire, rents a safe, green field for her dog Moscow twice a week.Moscow barks at bikes. He lunges at cars, children and other dogs. Lee knows that it is fear, not aggression. So taking him to a public park can only worsen the situation. Instead, she books a private field twice a week and lets him loose for an hour. This way, none of his triggers can get in. “Moscow is the world’s most difficult dog,” Lee told The Guardian. “If you’ve got a dog like him, who is reactive – he barks and lunges at stuff, mostly because he’s actually quite fearful – then every walk can be traumatic.”Lee isn’t the only pet parent to pay for a private park. In fact, this became increasingly common after the COVID-19 pandemic. Thousands of dog owners and pet parents across the country regularly hire private fields for their pets to run and exercise. And farmers like Ben Webster are making a living out of it!Sheep out, dogs inBen Webster, a farmer in Coton, near Cambridge, has watched that demand arrive at his gate. One of his fields used to be let for sheep grazing at £300 a year. So when this opportunity arrived at his doorstep, he spent £15,000 turning the field into a secure dog field. In the summer peak, it can now earn up to £400 a week. In other words, one good week beats a full year of sheep!“You get a whole mix of people. As well as the owners of dogs who are a bit nervous or not terribly well trained, you get dog-training classes. And you get people in the summer who want to just come, have a glass of wine in the field and let their dogs run around while they sit with friends on the bench and chat for an hour, knowing their dogs will be safe and secure,” Webster told the publication.The field comes with a tunnel to run through, tyres to jump over and a water tap. Some visitors also bring paddling pools for their dogs. “We had dog parties,” Webster said.For dogs like Moscow, this facility is a huge relief. The pup was born during the first lockdown and given up to a rescue centre by his previous owners when they stopped working from home. “He hadn’t had a lead or a collar on him until he was six months old. I don’t think he’d ever been walked on the pavement. And I think that led to a lot of his issues,” Lee recalls. She approached a dog behaviourist and has since started using a dog field near her home, which gives Moscow a safe space to play. “We are making lots of progress. He can now go on group walks with a dog walker and is great with other dogs he knows.”Ten pounds an hour, 756 fieldsWebster is one of many. There is a website dedicated to similar private dog fields. The website, dogwalkingfields.com, lists 756 fields covering an estimated 2,270 acres, with more added every week. An hour typically costs about £10, and the fields are usually fenced all round.“During the pandemic, enclosed fields became a refuge for people who wanted to exercise their dogs away from other people, socially distanced. Open spaces were crowded, especially with travel restrictions in place. As restrictions lifted a little, the fields became safe havens to meet up with friends and family and exercise safely,” Katherine Shields Smith, co-founder of Dog Walking Fields, said.The clientele stretches well beyond difficult dogs. Owners book for pets that are anxious, injured, disabled, small, elderly, in season or in training. “The owners of these dogs all appreciate somewhere safe to relax off-leash without being approached by other possibly well-meaning but exuberant dogs,” Shields Smith added.The unwelcome approach in public spaces is encouraging more and more pet parents to opt for such private fields. The pandemic only added to it. Many pandemic puppies were born into lockdown, when training classes were shut and owners kept their distance. Plenty have grown into poorly socialised adolescents with behaviour problems. Unwanted approaches in public can distress both dogs and owners. “There are lots of dogs who are friendly but whose owners have no control over them.” And for such pups, these private fields are a blessing. The same can be said for farmers like Webster.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: England turned a golf course into a wetland; 52,000 cubic metres of earth were moved and avocets are already breeding there
articles.summary: A former golf course on England's Lincolnshire coast has been transformed into a new wetland nature reserve, with ponds, open water, reedbeds, grassland
articles.body: A former golf course on England's Lincolnshire coast has been transformed into a new wetland nature reserve, with ponds, open water, reedbeds, grassland and coastal habitats replacing much of the former golfing landscape. Sandilands, near Sutton-on-Sea and Mablethorpe, opened to the public on September 26, 2026, following a six-year programme of planning, consultation and habitat creation led by the National Trust. The National Trust's latest press release describes the reserve as covering 30 hectares, although a September 2026 opening article by Visit Lincolnshire gives the area as 38 hectares, so the exact current area is not consistent across the organisations involved. What is not in dispute is the scale of the earthworks: nearly 52,000 cubic metres of earth were moved during the transformation. The project has already produced an early wildlife milestone, with avocet chicks hatching at Sandilands for the first time in July 2026.From a golf course dating to 1894 to a new coastal nature reserveThe Sandilands site has a long history as a golf course. The National Trust says the land was used for golf from 1894, while Sandilands Golf Club was formed in 1952. The club later entered liquidation in 2018, bringing its operation to an end. The National Trust acquired the former golf course in March 2020, using a supporter donation specifically directed towards Lincolnshire alongside funding from its Neptune Coastline Campaign. The acquisition marked the National Trust's first coastal land acquisition in Lincolnshire.The six-year project has involved converting the former golfing landscape into a mixture of wetland habitats, grassland and coastal scrub. The National Trust says the new reserve sits within the Lincolnshire Coastal Country Park and is intended to create more habitat for wildlife while improving public access to the coast. The project has also involved local partners, volunteers and public funding, including £2 million from the Mablethorpe Towns Fund through Connected Coast, £1.5 million from National Highways and £200,000 from the UK Government Shared Prosperity Fund, delivered by East Lindsey District Council.Nearly 52,000 cubic metres of earth were movedCreating the new landscape required extensive earthworks. According to the National Trust, nearly 52,000 cubic metres of earth were moved during the transformation. The charity compares that volume with 21 Olympic swimming pools or 11 Elizabeth Towers. The earthworks helped create ponds, open water and other wetland features across the former golf course.Planting has also been a major part of the project. The National Trust says more than 35,000 native coastal shrubs were planted across the wider project. Its project page separately records that more than 6,500 native scrub plants were planted with the help of more than 200 volunteers, including species such as hawthorn, sea buckthorn, blackthorn and wild rose. The National Trust says these plants will provide nectar, berries and nesting opportunities as they mature. Green hay collected from a nearby Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust reserve was also spread across parts of the site to help establish species-rich grassland. The National Trust identifies plants including wild carrot, yarrow, yellow rattle and red clover among the species associated with the developing grassland. The construction programme was planned around wildlife, with work carried out in stages to reduce disturbance during sensitive bird-breeding periods.Avocet chicks have already hatched at the new wetlandsThe new habitats are already being used by breeding birds. Avocet chicks hatched at Sandilands for the first time in July 2026, before the reserve officially opened to the public. The National Trust describes the arrival of the chicks as an encouraging sign that the newly created habitat is being used by wildlife. Visit Lincolnshire also reported that avocet chicks hatched at the site for the first time this year.The National Trust says Sandilands provides habitat for breeding birds including snipe, lapwing and oystercatcher, while uncommon migratory birds recorded or expected at the site include black-tailed godwit, spotted redshank and spoonbill. The latest National Trust press release describes Sandilands as part of the East Coast Flyway, an important migration route along Britain's eastern coastline. The charity says thousands of birds travel along the UK's east coast between Arctic and northern European breeding grounds and areas farther south. The National Trust has also highlighted species such as skylarks and meadow pipits, as well as rare plants including birdsfoot clover. The reserve is therefore intended to provide both breeding habitat for local species and places where migratory birds can stop during their journeys.A former golf course is now open for people and wildlifeThe transformation has also changed public access to the site. The former golf course has been replaced by a landscape with new paths and boardwalks through the developing wetland habitats. A visitor welcome building includes the Flyway Café, while accessible facilities include a Changing Places toilet. The National Trust says the new infrastructure is intended to make the coastal landscape easier for people to explore alongside the conservation work taking place there. The project is now moving from construction into the longer-term management of the reserve. The National Trust says Sandilands will continue to develop as its wetlands, grasslands and coastal vegetation mature. The first breeding avocets provide a documented early example of wildlife using the newly created habitat, but the ecological development of the reserve will continue to be monitored over the coming years.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ghana bans preaching on buses with jail terms for offenders
articles.summary: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.
articles.body:
Before the morning rush begins, the sound of praise and worship fills the Neoplan bus station in Ghana's capital, Accra, as a group of Christians gather to prepare to evangelise on vehicles taking travellers across the country.

Amid drumming and dancing, Boateng Bismark James leads 13 worshippers, nine men and four women, in prayer for drivers and passengers travelling to destinations across Ghana.

Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.

On long-distance buses, pastors can often be seen - and heard - preaching the gospel.

Sometimes they stand in the stairwell next to the driver, at others they walk up and down the aisle reading from the Bible and calling on sinners to repent at the tops of their voices. They do not stop even if the trip lasts for several hours.

The faithful sometimes offer money to the preachers to support their endeavours.

But a new law means this familiar practice could be coming to an end.

Anyone found preaching in public service vehicles faces up to eight months in prison, a fine of up to $52 (£39) or both.

The new regulation, passed by parliament in May, and which has started to be enforced in recent weeks, targets preaching and hawking on vehicles while they are in motion, classifying both as a nuisance and citing the safety and comfort of passengers.

Boateng, a 61-year-old pastor at Gospel Light church, has been preaching on commercial vehicles leaving Neoplan station since 2023.

"I preach on commercial vehicles because not everyone is able to go to church on Sunday. There are a lot of passengers who need our message of salvation to repent from their sins. We even heal the sick on some buses," he told the BBC in Twi, a local language.

Wearing a clerical collared shirt, Boateng moves through rows of buses loading passengers before boarding one bound for Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city.

We speak to him before the bus departs to avoid breaking the law.

Some travellers listen closely as he delivers his message. Others try to ignore him, browsing their phones, making calls or chatting among themselves.

"Some passengers are very happy with my message. Some even say they have never heard the message in church, but through my preaching they now know it is in the Bible," he says.

Critics say preaching on moving vehicles is a nuisance and a safety risk, as it could distract the driver, while supporters argue that evangelism is a Christian duty and should be protected under the freedom of religious worship.

One woman in her early 30s, who wishes to be identified as Chery Lokko, says she prefers to travel in peace.

''I don't like it because they are a nuisance. Some of them spit saliva on you unconsciously, especially if you are seated not far from them, and they are a nuisance in terms of noise and saliva. I like my peace whenever I'm on public transport.''

In one video widely shared on social media recently, a passenger on a minibus is seen angrily confronting a pastor attempting to board.

But in this devout country, ranked among the most religious in the world , others say evangelism on public transport is an important way of reaching people who may not attend church.

Bernice Nartey, a passenger travelling to Kumasi, says pastors should be allowed to preach, but only with passengers' consent.

"The preaching sometimes helps people to repent. For instance, if someone is going through a stressful situation, the message of the pastor can give the person renewed hope," she says.

Boateng says he was shaken by the regulation and wants religious preachers to be given an exemption.

"We are very worried, because most pastors here depend on preaching to take care of their families through the monetary gifts offered by passengers," he says.

"The government should allow us to preach on the buses and alight when it is exiting Accra," he adds.

For Boateng, preaching is not only a religious calling but also an important source of income.

"I have been able to take care of my children's education. My last-born just completed university, and half of the financial support came from money I got from preaching."

Ghana's constitution guarantees freedom of religion, although those rights are subject to considerations including public safety.

Preaching on commercial buses was first prohibited in Ghana in 2012, with offenders facing up to 30 days in prison.

But enforcement was weak and so the practice remained common, particularly on buses. The new law beefs up the penalties for those that flout the ban.

Preachers using megaphones can also often be seen and heard at Ghana's lorry parks and markets but they are not affected by the ban.

The Christian Council of Ghana did not respond to the BBC's request for a comment but Rev Enoch Paul Hayes, a senior pastor at one of the biggest churches in Ghana, the International Central Gospel Church, tells the BBC he does not think the new rules infringe on religious freedom.

He urges his fellow pastors not to break the law, saying they should find other ways of spreading their message.

"There is social media as an alternative outlet, where the same message can reach thousands of people," he says.

For Boateng and other bus preachers, the new rules create a difficult choice between adapting their ministry, giving up an important source of income, or risking falling foul of the law.

articles.summary: As he faces his ninth successive Knesset bid on Oct 27, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu is increasingly under scrutiny for his ‘failure’ to prevent the Oct
articles.body: As he faces his ninth successive Knesset bid on Oct 27, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu is increasingly under scrutiny for his ‘failure’ to prevent the Oct 7 massacre. In recent weeks, there has been a broad consensus inside and outside Israel that the Israeli govt, especially its intelligence establishment, failed to act on prior warnings from multiple sources, including Egypt, the UAE, and Palestinians. Arguments about the absence of ‘actionable intelligence’ do not hold water, especially with the families who lost their loved ones to incompetence and negligence.While Israel is known for last-minute electoral surprises, the picture is not rosy for Bibi. With more than 19 years in office, Bibi is already Israel’s longest-serving PM and has no intention of hanging up his boots anytime soon. Controversies and scandals are nothing new to him, and they date back to his first prime ministerial bid in May 1996. Unlike other elections in Israel and elsewhere, the forthcoming battle for the ballot does not center on the economy. Despite the war, the economy has recovered from the initial shock, thanks to high-tech resilience. With last week’s flydubai attempted hijack, the focus is on the proverbial security.There is a political-military divide in Israel over Oct 7. Several senior military and security officials took personal responsibility and left their posts prematurely. This has not been true of the political class. As the ultimate political authority, Netanyahu never took responsibility for the attack and avoided accountability. Initially, he delayed a formal inquiry, citing ‘ongoing war’, and then he hoped his ‘victory’ would weaken the demand for a judicial postmortem. His high-profile confrontation over controversial judicial reforms also contributed to his refusal.Under Israeli law and norms, a national inquiry commission into major crises is headed by the sitting president of the Israeli Supreme Court, equivalent to the Chief Justice of India. A similar inquiry into the October War of 1973 led to the resignation of PM Golda Meir, and she never returned to active politics. Naturally, Bibi has been averse to such judicial scrutiny.Unfortunately for him, as the Gaza and Iran conflicts dimmed, if not ended, demands for a national inquiry only grew. Indeed, all the major parties and leaders running in the election later this month are pledging a judicial inquiry into the failure. The field is also crowded with several former generals and intelligence figures who strongly disapprove of Bibi’s handling of Oct 7 and its aftermath. Hence, as much as he tries to avoid it, the massacre looms large over the electorate.Mainly due to the proportional system of elections, Israel has not had a single-party govt since 1948. Bibi is unlikely to secure even half of the majority mark. With his popularity falling, the latest opinion polls give Likud party only 18-21 seats, far fewer than the 32 seats it secured in the 2022 election.While he has established complete control over the ruling Likud, Bibi faces severe challenges from the right wing, which opposes even his minimalist accommodation of President Donald Trump’s Gaza Peace Plan. Otzma Yehudit (led by Itamar Ben-Gvir) and the Religious Zionist Party (headed by Bezalel Smotrich) oppose Bibi on the Gaza Strip and are projected to take a significant share of Likud’s voters.There are other significant contenders. Yashar, led by former general Gadi Eisenkot, is projected to be the largest party, expected to secure 21-25 seats. The rechristened ‘Together,’ the former Naftali Bennett-Yair Lapid coalition, could be another major player among centrist voters. Above all, the Democrats (the erstwhile Labour-Left coalition) are showing signs of revival and could garner some votes.For a long time, opposition disunity, the shrinking of the Left, and a strong alliance with the religious bloc have marked Bibi’s remarkable staying power. This time, the opposition is near-unanimous in rejecting Netanyahu’s refusal to be held accountable for Oct 7. If current projections hold and Likud loses more seats, Bibi’s post-election coalition-formation manoeuvring will be considerably weakened. Should the religious parties gain more seats, his dependence on the right-religious fringe will only increase.An election forecast is a dangerous gamble in Israel, and the signs are not very favourable for Bibi. Likud is unlikely to be the largest party in the next Knesset, but it could hold on to office with sufficient political concessions to the far right and economic incentives for the religious parties.As Israelis head to the polls just days after the third anniversary of the largest single act of terrorism in Israel’s history, Bibi might even do a political somersault and offer some form of judicial review of his role in the Oct 7 attack. Bibi, the proverbial comeback kid, could still spring a surprise and remain in office beyond Oct 27.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

Forensic evidence presented at the hearing included blood found on a garage mat that analysts said matched Rivas Hernandez’s DNA.Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said the evidence shown during the hearing represented only part of the prosecution’s case.“We believe that the evidence at trial will be overwhelming to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt on the three charges with which Mr. Burke will be charged,” Hochman told reporters outside the Los Angeles courthouse.D4vd faces three charges as defence maintains innocenceBurke faces first-degree murder, sexual abuse of a child and unlawful mutilation of human remains charges. articles.body: Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said Saturday that the institution "must do better" as it faces questions over its response to sexual assault allegations involving seven former fraternity brothers. "What happened to Jane Doe in 2024 is deeply disturbing and will weigh heavily on our community for years to come. My heart aches when I think of what she experienced," Kotlikoff said in a video statement to the Cornell community. Kotlikoff said the case raises questions about sexual assault, campus party culture, alcohol and drug abuse on the Ithaca, New York, campus, as well as the investigation conducted after the allegations were reported. "I want to acknowledge something that can be difficult for an institution to say we don't have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves. I believe we as an administration, and we as a community must do better," Kotlikoff said. INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM Kotlikoff welcomed an independent review by an outside law firm into Cornell's handling of the case and said the university supports Gov. Kathy Hochul's decision to turn the criminal investigation over to New York Attorney General Letitia James. He said Cornell would not wait for those reviews to conclude before making changes to prevention and education, student support, mental health and substance use resources and investigative processes. "We will act," Kotlikoff said.Jane Doe alleges in a lawsuit that seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers drugged and sexually assaulted her during an October 2024 night at the fraternity house. Doe was a 20-year-old Cornell undergraduate at the time. CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS PROMPT NY ATTORNEY GENERAL LETITIA JAMES TO OPEN ‘ACTIVE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION’ The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men. Doe filed a 101-page lawsuit last month accusing the former fraternity members of sexual assault and rape and naming Cornell and other entities. The case came under renewed scrutiny after Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office had not received the full transcript of Doe's November 2024 interview with Cornell University Police before prosecutors initially declined to pursue charges. Van Houten reopened the investigation before Hochul appointed the Office of the Attorney General as special prosecutor. James said Friday that her office was conducting an "active criminal investigation." CORNELL SEXUAL ASSAULT CASE REVIVES SCRUTINY OF A LITTLE-KNOWN NEW YORK LAW ON INTOXICATED VICTIMS Kotlikoff also addressed frustration over Cornell's communication about its response to the allegations and said the university would make a greater effort to be transparent. "There are real legal and privacy limits on what we can say, but we will make a greater effort to explain what we can to provide context about the actions Cornell has taken and to be more transparent," Kotlikoff said. articles.title: Tennessee prison chief Frank Strada resigns after Christa Pike's botched execution; governor orders review
articles.summary: Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada will resign this month following the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike,
articles.body: Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada will resign this month following the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike, Governor Bill Lee announced Saturday, as the state faces growing calls for answers over the second botched execution attempt in five months.Lee also appointed former US Attorney Ed Stanton to lead an independent review of what went wrong during Pike's execution attempt on Wednesday. The governor has halted further executions while the review is under way.Strada said his resignation was “in the best interest of Tennesseans” while the review is conducted. He defended the state's execution process, saying he believed Tennessee “carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol.”Pike, 50, remained unconscious and on a ventilator in hospital after the state administered two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital but failed to complete her execution. Her lawyers said hospital staff were trying to clear the drug from her system. There was no immediate update on her condition from her legal team on Saturday.Pike's lawyers welcomed Strada's departure but said it “does nothing to help Christa now.”“What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person,” the four-lawyer team said. “We hope the governor’s call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee’s entire death penalty system.”Problems with IV lines blamedThe execution attempt has drawn criticism from both supporters and opponents of the death penalty. Pike's lawyers said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to enter her body rather than her bloodstream.Pike was reportedly cooperative as the execution team struggled to insert the IV lines. Her lawyer Randy Spivey said she even told staff, “please try here, please try here” as they attempted to place the lines.Second failed execution since MayThe incident was the second time since May that Tennessee stopped an execution after a prisoner appeared to be close to death. In May, officials halted the execution of Tony Carruthers after they managed to place an IV in his right arm but could not establish a second line. Lee later ordered that Carruthers not be executed again for at least a year.Stanton has previously reviewed problems with Tennessee's lethal injection process. In 2022, Lee appointed him to examine why another execution was called off. Stanton concluded that the state had failed to follow its own lethal injection procedures.Strada's record in Tennessee and ArizonaStrada became commissioner of Tennessee's Department of Correction in January 2023 after serving as deputy director of the Arizona Department of Corrections. In late 2024, he announced that Tennessee would change its lethal injection protocol and use only pentobarbital.His record in Arizona has also come under scrutiny. Court filings show that Strada oversaw executions there when the state resumed carrying them out in 2022 after an eight-year pause.During the execution of Clarence Dixon that year, medical staff struggled to find a vein and eventually made an incision in his groin to administer the drugs. The process lasted about 25 minutes.Medical staff also initially struggled to find a vein during Frank Atwood's execution in 2022 before inserting an IV into his right hand. During Murray Hooper's execution later that year, an attempt to place an IV in his right arm failed, while a line inserted in his leg entered his femoral artery.“When Governor Lee hired Strada to fix execution problems in Tennessee, his problematic history of executions in Arizona was well known,” said Kit Thomas, an attorney who has represented people on Tennessee's death row.You use AI every day. articles.title: UK weather: Autumn chill to arrive as temperatures finally drop
articles.summary: After highs of 28C in the final week of September, cooler air will arrive this week with temperatures falling closer to the seasonal norm.
articles.body:
Temperatures are set to drop across the UK during the week ahead, bringing an end to a run of warmer-than-average autumn weather.

By Wednesday, afternoon highs are expected to range from 11C (52F) in northern Scotland to 17C (63C) in southern England.

It will mark a significant change from the summer-like warmth that has brought temperatures of up to 28C over the last week.

If the thermometer fails to reach 20C anywhere in the UK, it will be the first time that has happened since 11 June.

Mild end to weekend before temperatures tumble

In south Wales, the Midlands, East Anglia and southern England, early mist and fog could linger for a while in a few locations on Sunday.

However, once this clears sunny spells are expected.

More cloud will develop in north Wales and northern England with the chance of a few spots of rain.

Northern Ireland will be even cloudier, with some outbreaks of mainly light rain and drizzle.

The wettest weather will be found across Scotland with heavy rain likely in the west, accompanied by wind gusts of 40mph or more in the far north-west.

Temperatures will generally be a few degrees above the seasonal norm and could possibly reach 23C in the sunniest parts of southern England.

A weather front will erratically move southwards during Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.

This will bring outbreaks of rain which will generally be heaviest in northern and western parts of the UK and lighter further east.

It is possible that heavier downpours with thunder and lightning could affect southern and south-eastern England on Tuesday night and Wednesday.

As the rain clears southwards cooler air will be left in its wake with daytime temperatures by midweek expected to be at - or even slightly below - the seasonal average.

Some chilly nights are also expected with a touch of frost possible in prone locations.

With meteorological autumn covering the months of September, October and November, the season is now one-third of the way over.

Met Office figures show that it has been a warmer-than-normal autumn so far, with September being the joint-fourth warmest on record for the UK as a whole.

With a mean average temperature of 14.6C, it was 1.6C above the long-term average.

The longer-range prospects for autumn predict more of the same.

It is forecast to be warmer and wetter than average with the chance of stormy weather later in the season - partly due to the developing very strong El Niño in the Pacific.

The UK is on track for one of its warmest years on record, according to the Met Office.
